facts.claim: IATA said at the opening of the IATA World Financial Symposium and World Passenger Symposium in Macao that the challenge is turning digitalization advances across airline retailing, payments and digital identity into better passenger journeys and a more efficient, financially resilient industry.

IATA's Interim Director General Sandrine Le Borgne said travelers can already use AI to plan trips, pay with digital wallets and use biometrics for a more seamless airport journey, and the challenge now is realizing the value these innovations can create.

AI assistants and automated agents are changing how travelers discover and compare travel, and airlines should prepare for this shift while retaining control of their data and commercial relationships and ensuring data quality.

Seven airlines are live or implementing Orders under Modern Airline Retailing, more than 20 are expected to follow from 2027, and IT providers have committed more than US$1.7 billion to Offers and Orders.

Airlines spend more than US$24.5 billion annually to process payments, and new payment methods affect customer choice, cost, cash flow and risk, so financial functions must be considered as part of digitalization investment.

Biometrics are increasingly part of normal travel and make airport processing faster, but many solutions are airport- or country-specific, so their full value for passengers and airlines is not yet realized.

The standards for secure digital passports exist with ICAO's Digital Travel Credential, more than eight in ten passengers are interested in using a digital passport to check in, and wider adoption depends on governments issuing and accepting digital travel credentials.
The 2026 WFS and WPS are the first editions of these events held in North Asia, and China's airlines carried more than 770 million passengers in 2025, a record high.
IATA represents over 370 airlines accounting for some 85% of global air traffic.

zh.title: IATA點出數位化三大優先課題：航空零售、支付與數位身分須轉化為實質價值
zh.summary: 國際航空運輸協會在澳門舉行的世界金融研討會暨世界旅客研討會開幕時指出，航空業的挑戰是把航空零售、支付與數位身分等數位化進展，轉化為更順暢的旅客旅程與更有效率、財務更具韌性的產業；現代航空零售已有7家航空公司上線或導入Orders，IT業者並已承諾投入逾17億美元。
body: 國際航空運輸協會在澳門舉行的世界金融研討會暨世界旅客研討會開幕時指出，旅客如今已能運用人工智慧規劃行程、以數位錢包付款並以生物辨識讓機場流程更順暢，航空業接下來的挑戰是實現這些創新能創造的價值，讓旅行更有效率並提升財務韌性。人工智慧助理與自動化代理正在改變旅客搜尋與比價的方式，航空公司一方面要為此轉變做好準備，一方面也要保有對自身資料、商業關係的主導權並確保資料品質。

在航空零售方面，現代航空零售是因應市場變化的核心，已有7家航空公司上線或正在導入Orders，預計2027年起逾20家跟進，資訊科技業者也已承諾投入逾17億美元於Offers與Orders。在支付方面，航空公司每年支付處理成本逾245億美元，新的支付方式會影響旅客選擇、成本、現金流與風險，相關的對帳、清算與收益會計必須從轉型之初就納入規劃，而非只是把既有流程數位化。生物辨識方面，雖然已漸成常態並加快機場處理速度，但多數方案仍限於特定機場或國家，價值尚未充分實現；國際民航組織的數位旅行憑證標準已經存在，逾八成旅客也有興趣以數位護照辦理報到，普及的關鍵在於各國政府願意核發並接受數位旅行憑證。本屆研討會是首度在北亞舉行，中國航空公司2025年載客逾7.7億人次、創下新高。

en.title: IATA sets digitalization priorities: retailing, payments and digital identity must create real value
en.summary: At the opening of the IATA World Financial Symposium and World Passenger Symposium in Macao, IATA said the industry's challenge is turning digitalization advances in airline retailing, payments and digital identity into smoother passenger journeys and a more efficient, financially resilient industry; seven airlines are live or implementing Orders, with IT providers committing more than US$1.7 billion to Offers and Orders.
body: The International Air Transport Association said at the opening of the IATA World Financial Symposium and World Passenger Symposium in Macao that travelers can already use AI to plan trips, pay with digital wallets and use biometrics for a more seamless airport journey, and that the challenge now is realizing the value these innovations can create to make travel more efficient and improve financial resilience. AI assistants and automated agents are changing how travelers discover and compare travel, and airlines should prepare for this shift while retaining control of their data and commercial relationships and ensuring the quality of the underlying data.

Modern Airline Retailing is central to adapting to this changing marketplace: seven airlines are live or implementing Orders, more than 20 are expected to follow from 2027, and IT providers have committed more than US$1.7 billion to Offers and Orders. On payments, airlines spend more than US$24.5 billion annually to process payments, and new payment methods affect customer choice, cost, cash flow and risk, so reconciliation, settlement and revenue accounting must be built into the transformation from the start rather than simply digitizing existing complexity. Biometrics are increasingly part of normal travel and make airport processing faster, but many solutions are airport- or country-specific, so their full value is not yet realized; the standards for secure digital passports exist with ICAO's Digital Travel Credential, more than eight in ten passengers are interested in using a digital passport to check in, and wider adoption depends on governments issuing and accepting digital travel credentials. The 2026 events are the first editions held in North Asia, and China's airlines carried more than 770 million passengers in 2025, a record high.
